ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Common, TargetType.Self)` (Havoc.cs:14-17) == cost 1 / SKILL / COMMON / SELF. Havoc has no Exhaust keyword of its own -- the hover tip (Havoc.cs:12) refers to the card it exhausts -- and the sim leaves `exhausts` False.

OnPlay.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-27 (partly closed). CLOSED: the RNG-stream half. `havoc.py:59-61` now picks the auto-play target with `ctx.combat.combat_rng.targets.choice(living)` instead of `ctx.combat._rng.choice(living)`, which is CardCmd.cs:77's stream; the card no longer appears in `py audit/tools/card_probes.py shared-rng` (20 classes, havoc not among them). STILL OPEN, and this is what the gap now is: Havoc still calls `card.on_play(ctx, idx)` directly (havoc.py:52, 62) instead of routing through `CombatState.auto_play_card`, so it still skips the entire play bracket that `_resolve_card_play` provides (combat.py:520-620, re-read today) -- `hooks.on_energy_spent(card, 0)` (combat.py:657, so Free Attack and every other BeforeCardPlayed listener never fires), the per-play-index `before_card_played` / `after_card_played` bracket, the play-count loop seeded from `1 + card.base_replay_count` (combat.py:553-554, so a Spiral-enchanted or Hidden-Gem'd card plays ONCE instead of twice), the `before_attack` / `after_attack` bracket (Vigor from Akabeko is not consumed), the in-loop `EnchantmentModel.OnPlay` call (combat.py:592-593), and `captured_x` for X-cost cards (combat.py:547-549, so a Whirlwind auto-played by Havoc still does nothing). C#'s `CardPileCmd.AutoPlayFromDrawPile` reaches `OnPlayWrapper` and runs the full bracket (Havoc.cs:21 -> CardCmd.cs:129). The bracket half got LARGER, not smaller, in the fix campaign: `_resolve_card_play` now runs BeforeCardPlayed and AfterCardPlayed once per play index rather than once per logical play, so Havoc drops more per auto-play than it did when this entry was written. LIVE: Havoc is a ported Common and Akabeko, Hidden Gem, the Spiral enchantment and X-cost cards are all ported. The fix shape is unchanged -- pull the card off the draw pile, then call `ctx.combat.auto_play_card(card)`, as card/cascade does. HISTORY -- WHAT THE DIVERGENCE WAS: C# is a single line: `CardPileCmd.AutoPlayFromDrawPile(choiceContext, Owner, 1, CardPilePosition.Top, forceExhaust: true)` (Havoc.cs:21). The sim reimplements the whole verb inline AND, unlike card/cascade -- which reimplements the same verb faithfully -- it does not route the play through `CombatState.auto_play_card`. It calls `card.on_play(ctx, idx)` directly (havoc.py:52, 57), which SKIPS the entire play bracket that `_resolve_card_play` provides (combat.py:441-513): `hooks.on_energy_spent(card, 0)` (so Free Attack and any other BeforeCardPlayed listener never fires -- C#'s AutoPlay reaches `OnPlayWrapper` and runs the full bracket, CardCmd.cs:129), `hooks.before_card_played`, the play-count loop from `modify_card_play_count` (so a Spiral-enchanted or Hidden-Gem'd card plays ONCE instead of twice), the `before_attack`/`after_attack` bracket (so Vigor from Akabeko is not consumed), and `captured_x` for X-cost cards (so a Whirlwind auto-played by Havoc does nothing). It also picks the random target with `ctx.combat._rng.choice(living)` (havoc.py:56) -- the unseeded shared rng -- where `auto_play_card` correctly uses `self.combat_rng.targets` with the CardCmd.cs:77 citation in-line (combat.py:540-546), so Havoc is also one of the 21 cards the `shared-rng` probe lists. LIVE on every count: Havoc is a ported Common, and Akabeko, Hidden Gem, the Spiral enchantment and X-cost cards are all ported. The fix shape is the one card/cascade already uses -- pull the card off the draw pile, then call `ctx.combat.auto_play_card(card)`. Presentation: none in the C# body. REGRESSION TEST: `test/test_rng_tripwire.py:33` (`test_no_wrong_stream_draws_in_random_run`, 20 seeded full runs) is the standing gate for this whole family. It wraps `RunState.rng` and asserts ZERO in-combat draws on it; `CombatState` receives that same object as `self._rng` (run.py:1146-1148, combat.py:88), so a `ctx.combat._rng` draw taken from inside a card's `on_play` is recorded and fails the gate -- verified by playing this family's shape under a `Tripwire` and getting a hit at the `card.on_play` frame (combat.py:490). The gate is green today, so these 20 seeds never reach this card's draw; routing the site to the named `combat_rng` accessor is verified by keeping it green.

guards.rationale: Faithful to `AutoPlayFromDrawPile`'s per-iteration `ShuffleIfNecessary` (CardPileCmd.cs:941) and its `FirstOrDefault()` top-of-pile pick (945): the sim reshuffles only when the draw pile is empty and the discard is not, uses the named `combat_rng.shuffle` stream, fires `on_shuffle`, and pops the END of its draw pile, which is its top. Returning early when both piles are empty matches C#'s `cardModel == null` break (949-952).

guards.what: `forceExhaust: true` is reproduced by appending to the exhaust pile directly (havoc.py:62-64)
guards.issue: C# sets `item.ExhaustOnNextPlay = forceExhaust` (CardPileCmd.cs:960) and lets the play pipeline route the card to the exhaust pile, which means the card passes through PileType.Play first and lands in Exhaust through `CardPileCmd.Add`. The sim appends straight to `exhaust_pile` and fires `on_card_exhausted`, skipping the result-pile redirect hook (`modify_card_play_result_pile`, combat.py:505-509 -- Nostalgia) that C# would consult. DORMANT: Nostalgia redirects Attack/Skill plays to the top of the DRAW pile, and C#'s ExhaustOnNextPlay takes precedence over the result-pile choice, so the two agree today; live if a ported result-pile modifier ever outranks a forced exhaust. Recorded separately from the OnPlay entry because it is a distinct mechanism.
